paper.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs

summary.one_sentence: Gorilla turns API use into a retrieval-aware function-calling problem: pick the right API from a large changing catalog, generate a valid call, and avoid hallucinated tools.
summary.thesis: Tool use at API-catalog scale requires more than prompting: the model needs APIBench-style training data, retrieval-aware finetuning, and structural evaluation that distinguishes wrong calls from invented APIs.
summary.why_it_matters: Gorilla makes API documentation and catalog freshness part of the agent stack. The model is not only choosing an action; it is choosing from a mutable registry whose entries, arguments, versions, and constraints change over time.

prior_state: Prompted LLMs could call small, well-described tool sets, but the prompt context cannot hold web-scale API catalogs.
State-of-the-art models such as GPT-4 still made wrong API calls or hallucinated nonexistent API usage.
API calls are hard to evaluate with ordinary unit tests because many APIs can be functionally similar and many arguments are optional.
problem.key_gap: The paper asks how to train and evaluate an LLM that maps natural-language goals to correct API calls across a large, overlapping, frequently updated API corpus.
assumptions: API documentation can be normalized into structured records with fields such as API name, call, arguments, requirements, examples, performance, and description.
Synthetic instructions can be generated from API documentation using self-instruct.
A retriever can provide candidate API documentation at inference time, but may retrieve irrelevant or stale documentation.
The target output is a single API call or small code snippet rather than a complete multi-step program.

concepts.name: APIBench
concepts.definition: A benchmark and training corpus of API documentation plus synthetic instruction/API pairs from TorchHub, TensorHub, and HuggingFace APIs.

concepts.name: Retriever-aware training
concepts.definition: Instruction finetuning where retrieved API documentation is appended to the prompt so the model learns to use relevant docs and ignore irrelevant ones.

concepts.name: AST subtree matching
concepts.definition: An evaluation method that parses generated API code and checks whether the relevant call and arguments match a subtree in the reference API database.

method.core_idea: Collect API documentation from model hubs, generate instruction/API pairs with self-instruct, finetune a LLaMA-7B model into Gorilla with and without retrieved documentation, and evaluate generated calls using AST subtree matching plus hallucination/error accounting.
action_grammar: User instruction: a natural-language request for an ML model or API capability.
API document: a structured record containing domain, provider, API call, arguments, requirements, example code, performance, and description.
Retriever: BM25, GPT-Index, or oracle retrieval over API documents.
Gorilla response: domain, API provider, API call, explanation, and optional supporting code.
Hallucination: an API call that is not a subtree of any API in the database.
Error: a non-hallucinated but incorrect API choice or argument match.
steps: Curate API documentation from TorchHub, TensorHub, and HuggingFace.
Generate synthetic user instructions and reference API answers with self-instruct.
Convert each example into a one-turn user/agent instruction-tuning conversation.
Optionally append retrieved API documentation to the user prompt for retriever-aware training.
At inference, run Gorilla zero-shot or append top retrieved API documentation.
Evaluate the generated API call by AST subtree matching against the API database.
method.pseudocode:
api_docs = collect_model_hub_docs()
examples = self_instruct(api_docs)
for example in examples:
    prompt = example.instruction
    if retriever_aware:
        prompt += retrieve_oracle_doc(example.api)
    train_pair = chat(prompt, example.reference_api_call)
finetune(llama_7b, train_pairs)

query_doc = retrieve(user_query)
call = gorilla(user_query, query_doc)
score = ast_subtree_match(call, reference_api_database)

claims.statement: APIBench covers 1,645 ML APIs across TorchHub, TensorHub, and HuggingFace, with 10 generated instructions per API for 16,450 instruction/API pairs.
claims.scope: Section 3.1 and Appendix A.1 in the accepted paper.
caveats: The API corpus is ML-centric, not a general web API corpus.

claims.statement: Gorilla is a LLaMA-7B model instruction-finetuned for API calls, with retriever-aware training that teaches it to use or ignore retrieved API documentation.
caveats: RAT depends on retrieval quality; the paper explicitly reports that bad retrieval can hurt.

claims.statement: The paper evaluates API-call correctness with AST subtree matching and defines hallucination as a generated API call that matches no API in the database.
caveats: AST matching is a structural offline proxy; the paper separately samples manual execution because executing every generated call is impractical.

claims.statement: In zero-shot API generation, Gorilla reports higher overall accuracy and lower hallucination than GPT-4 across TorchHub, HuggingFace, and TensorHub in Table 1.
caveats: For HuggingFace, the paper notes that non-Gorilla models are evaluated on correct domain names because the dataset is not exhaustive.

claims.statement: Retriever-aware training can adapt to test-time documentation changes and improves with strong retrievers, but weak retrieval at inference can sharply degrade accuracy.
caveats: The strongest retrieval results use oracle retrieval, which is an upper bound rather than a deployed retriever.

claims.statement: Gorilla focuses on selecting and generating single API calls for ML APIs; API execution, multi-step tool workflows, and general web API side effects are outside the main paper scope.
claims.scope: Methodology, inference note, Appendix dataset/task definition, and limitations/social impact section.
caveats: This is still a strong benchmark for function-calling correctness, but not a full agent runtime benchmark.

evidence.result: The accepted paper describes 1,645 API calls: 94 from TorchHub, 626 from TensorHub, and 925 from HuggingFace, with 10 generated instructions per API, yielding 16,450 instruction/API pairs.
evidence.metric: API count and instruction/API pair count

evidence.result: Gorilla is a retriever-aware finetuned LLaMA-7B model. During RAT, the prompt includes retrieved API documentation, and the model is trained to use relevant documentation or fall back to learned API knowledge when retrieval is irrelevant.

Generated API calls are parsed into ASTs and matched against reference API subtrees. A sampled manual check reports 78% AST accuracy, 78% human-evaluated API accuracy, and 72% executable supporting code.

In zero-shot mode, Gorilla scores 59.13 TorchHub, 71.68 HuggingFace, and 83.79 TensorHub overall accuracy with hallucination rates 6.98, 10.95, and 5.40. GPT-4 zero-shot scores 38.70, 19.80, and 18.20 accuracy with hallucination rates 36.55, 37.16, and 78.65.

With oracle retrieval, RAT-trained Gorilla reaches 67.20 TorchHub, 91.26 HuggingFace, and 94.16 TensorHub overall accuracy. The paper also reports that using non-oracle retrieval at evaluation can produce large degradation, including 29.20% for GPT-Index and 52.27% for BM25 in one comparison.

The accepted paper shows Gorilla responding to test-time documentation changes such as upgrading FCN from ResNet-50 to ResNet-101 and changing the model registry from pytorch/vision to NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples:torchhub.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2 inference note, Appendix A.1, Appendix A.1 API Call Task, Section 6
evidence.result: The paper says API execution exists but is not the focus, defines the API-call task as generating a single line of code or leveraging an API reference, and notes that the dataset is ML API focused.

agent_infra_takeaways: API catalogs are first-class infrastructure. Agent quality depends on normalized docs, versioning, retriever freshness, and schema fields for arguments and constraints.
Function-calling evaluation needs structural checks. AST subtree matching separates invented APIs from wrong-but-existing APIs more cleanly than text similarity.
Retrieval is not automatically helpful. A runtime must measure retriever precision and teach models when to ignore irrelevant retrieved documentation.
Hallucination should be typed. Gorilla distinguishes nonexistent tools from incorrect API choices, which maps naturally to different remediation paths.
Constraint handling belongs in the API schema: performance, parameter count, latency, cost, and requirements need to be queryable if agents must choose among tools.
This is a tool-selection layer, not an execution runtime. Side effects, permissions, retries, rollback, and multi-step plans still need separate infrastructure.
caveats: The core benchmark is centered on ML APIs, not arbitrary REST, SaaS, or operating-system APIs.
The main task generates one API call or small code snippet rather than a full multi-step workflow.
Oracle retrieval is an upper bound; BM25 and GPT-Index retrieval can degrade accuracy when irrelevant docs are appended.
AST matching checks structural API-call equivalence and does not prove complete program execution for every output.
For HuggingFace, non-Gorilla baseline evaluation is relaxed because the API set is not exhaustive.
The work does not solve side-effect safety, authentication, authorization, or sandboxing for real API execution.

related_work.title: Toolformer
related_work.note: Toolformer teaches a model to emit calls for a small fixed tool set; Gorilla moves toward large API catalogs, retrieval, and hallucination measurement.

related_work.title: ToolLLM
related_work.note: ToolLLM scales from API-call selection toward multi-step real-world API trajectories and search over tool-use sequences.

related_work.title: Model Context Protocol
related_work.note: MCP addresses the protocol and interoperability layer that Gorilla's API-catalog setting makes operationally important.

poc.note: No PoC yet - contributions welcome. A useful local PoC would build a tiny APIBench-style catalog, generate candidate API calls from natural-language requests, and score them with AST subtree matching.
